newsitem.title: UK: L&G profits rise, sees strong div growth.
newsitem.headline: L&G profits rise, sees strong div growth.

text.p: British insurance group Legal and General Group Plc on Thursday reported a 15.4 percent rise in operating profits from continuing operations in 1996 to 291.4 million pounds ($465.4 million) and predicted strong dividend growth goping forward.

"Our commitment to provide consistently competitive products has produced excellent sales growth and good profit growth. Through this virtuous circle, Legal & General will continue to be a strong performer," said chief executive David Prosser.
Profits from life and pensions businesses rose nearly 14 percent to 250 million pounds.
The dividend for the year was also raised 14 percent to 11.13 pence per share.
The results included an exceptional profit of 70 million pounds for the sale of the company's commercial lines business.

Prosser said the core UK life and pensions business had profitably grown market share in very competitive conditions and the results demonstrated the success of the group's strategy of providing competitive products through a range of distribution channels.
